input.summary:
P0 dining room furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: oak-fence and top-slab table along x11 with three stair chairs on the window side, a barrel sideboard with a potted poppy, a hanging lantern and two lit candles over the table. Walk 9/9 reachable and light min 10, no dark cell, in an unlocked test copy (room3-test.nbt) that `mcd room` reports OK.
Real make.sh does not land it: shell-west.mjs:16 and :20 fill the whole interior with air, so runParts locks all 14 of my writes (REFUSED).
left: BLOCKER (not my module): parts/shell-west.mjs:16 and :20 fill the interior air with g.fill(..., "air"), which marks every cell of the P0 dining box (and every other room box) as owned by an earlier part, so runParts refuses all 14 furniture writes in the real build. Fix belongs to the shell owner: drop the interior air fill (unset cells are already air) and keep the openings carve at line 23. Once that lands, make.sh should show 14 placed for this part with no REFUSED.
Verified only on room3-test.nbt (build.nbt with the box cells unset, made by a one-off node script), not on the real build.nbt; room.png was rendered from that test copy.

Hearth: the brief says the E hearth is at (12,2,17), but plan.md puts the mouth at the wall cell (13,2,17) with the fire outside. I kept (12,2,17) clear as the hearth front; the grounds/chimney part owns the fire.
plan.md's checklist (parts 1-6) and elements.md have no room-level item for this room; the row-wide 'Per house: dining table' line is shared with the other rooms, so I did not tick it.

waste.what: Found the cause of 14 REFUSED writes by reading build.mjs's lock and shell-west.mjs by hand, then wrote a one-off node script to unset my box and save a test copy so the room check could run.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and roughly 3 minutes
waste.tool: A `mcd room --unlock-box` or a runParts option to report which earlier part owns each locked cell (e.g. 'shell-west.mjs:16 fill air') would have pointed at the shell fill at once, and would let a room designer check their furniture without a copy.

waste.what: Hand-drew the furniture into three separate layers() calls with the row shape guessed; the first attempt wrapped each row in its own array, so the table posts landed one row off and only the floor grid showed it.
waste.cost: one wrong write pass plus one rewrite, ~2 minutes
waste.tool: layers() should reject a row list whose length or nesting does not match the origin/size, or echo back the cells it wrote as a grid so the layout is checked as text.

waste.what: Worked out lantern and candle positions and the walkable lanes cell by cell (x10 z15..17, x11 z17, x12 z17) from the plan grid, then checked light by eye against the room check.
waste.tool: `mcd plan --rooms` could print the proposed lanes and the doorway first cells as a mark on the grid, so a designer sees the protected cells before drawing.

companions.task: Remove the interior air fill at shell-west.mjs lines 16 and 20 so the room boxes are not locked as earlier-part cells; keep the wall builds and the openings carve at line 23. This unblocks every room part, not only the dining room.

Check the lantern and two candles over the table against the whole-house light map once the walls and glazing are in, to confirm the dining room stays at 8+ with the windows open and the window-side chairs placed.
